== Problem ==

Sekou writes the numbers <imath>15, 16, 17, 18, 19.</imath> After he erases one of his numbers, the sum of the remaining four numbers is a multiple of <imath>4.</imath> Which number did he erase?

<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ 15\qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 16\qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 17\qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 18\qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 19</imath>
== Solution 1 ==

The sum of all five numbers is <imath>85. Since </imath>85 is <imath>1 more than a multiple of </imath>4, the number being subtracted must be <imath> 1 more than a multiple of </imath><imath>. Thus, the answer is </imath>\boxed{\text{(C)}~17}$. ~Gavin_Deng

== Solution 2 - Creativity 💡==

Notice the <imath>10</imath>'s place as you erase one number; you get <imath>40</imath>, which is a multiple of <imath>4</imath>, so you can ignore the <imath>10</imath>'s place in the numbers provided altogether because it will always be a multiple of 40. This means that the only relevant numbers are the <imath>1</imath>'s digit ones. If you add the numbers now, you get <imath>5+6+7+8+9=35.</imath> The closest multiple of <imath>4</imath> underneath <imath>35</imath> which can be achieved as a result of subtracting either <imath>5</imath>, <imath>6</imath>, <imath>7</imath>, <imath>8</imath>, or <imath>9</imath> is <imath>28</imath>, which is achieved by subtracting <imath>7</imath>, therefore the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}~17}</imath>.

~firethinkz

== Solution 3 ==
The sum of the residues of these numbers modulo <imath>4</imath> is <imath>-1+0+1+2+3=5 \equiv 1 \pmod 4</imath>. Hence, the number being subtracted must be congruent to <imath>1</imath> modulo <imath>4</imath>. The only such answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}~17}</imath>.

\(\textbf{Note}\): To those who are confused about why, for <imath>15</imath>, it said the residue modulo <imath>4</imath> is <imath>-1</imath>  instead of <imath>3</imath> (because of <imath>12</imath>), look here. <imath>-1 \equiv 3 \pmod 4</imath>. The same principle above applies even if you replace <imath>-1</imath> with <imath>3</imath>; two numbers are in the same residue class if their difference is a multiple of the modulus ( \(3-(-1)=4\), which is \(1\times 4\) ). 

~cxsmi

~note by i_am_not_suk_at_math

== Solution 4 ==
The sum of all the numbers here is equivalent to <imath>17 \cdot 5</imath>. Subtracting 17 gives us <imath>17 \cdot 4</imath>, which is clearly a multiple of 4. Therefore, the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}~17}</imath>.
~themathkidwoohooooo

== Solution 5 ==

Since the sum of <imath>15 + \dots + 19</imath> is odd, we immediately exclude B and D. We further note that if A is true, then E is true. Hence, the answer is C.  

== Solution 6==

We can use the fact that <imath>(a + b) \mod n = [(a \mod n) + (b \mod n)] \mod n</imath>. Notice that <imath>15, 16, 17, 18, 19</imath> dividing by 4 have remainders <imath>3, 0, 1, 2, 3</imath>. Their sum is 9. It is easy to see that <imath>9-1=8</imath> is divisible by 4 and so <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}~17}</imath> is the correct answer.

~minor edit by themathkidwoohooooo, just fixed the LaTeX for the answer

==Solution 7==

If we use brute force and add <imath>15+16+17+18+19</imath>, we get <imath>85</imath>. When we subtract every number from <imath>85</imath>, we get <imath>70</imath>, <imath>69</imath>, <imath>68</imath>, <imath>67</imath>, <imath>66</imath>, we see that <imath>68</imath> is divisible by <imath>4</imath>, so <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}~17}</imath> is the correct answer.

~VersatileGopher38
